en: Now, O Śiva, the wise describe the worship that is specific to all [deities] in brief, preceded by the general procedure. ||1||
Then, standing facing north at the conclusion of the sacrifice and other rites, the wise man, having burnt the body consisting of bonds with the fire of the *praṇava*, [proceeds]. || 2 ||
One should meditate upon the all-pervading, subtle Self, whose essence is the Praṇava;
one should contemplate its body, which consists of the portions of Brahman, in successive order. || 3 ||
There, having first formed the salutation-mudrā, one should contemplate;
with five [fingers] one should perform the five [limbs], and with the fifth [finger] one should perform the head.
Then, having bound the five mudrās, one should contemplate the four faces with the fourth mantra, which is composed of the digits (kalā).
One who knows the application [of the technique] should contemplate the harsh [vowel], which has five forms, in five ways:
the knower of divisions should contemplate it in the heart, the neck, the shoulders, and the back.
Having bound the vāmadeva in nine ways, one should fix the śaśakarṇikā upon the liṅga, the anus, the thighs, the knees, and likewise the feet.
The practitioner of mantra should likewise place the mantra, ending with the word of salutation (namas), upon the calves, as well as on the left and right sides.
Then, having formed the mukulī-mudrā, the wise meditator should contemplate the Self as Sadyojāta in five ways, as one whose nature is composed of the [five] kalās.
Having likewise fashioned the feet, hands, arms, nose, and head as before, one should then place Śiva in the locus of the object.
One who knows the application of the Śiva-mudrā and understands the divisions of the abode of Śiva should thereafter place the Universal Self within the heart by means of the Śāntā [mudrā]. || 11 ||
Having placed Suśiva on the head by means of the mantra known as Liṅga,
one should then contemplate Jvālinī upon the topknot by means of the Dhvaja-mantra.
One should place [the deity], radiant as the sun, upon that limb with the *āvāhinī* mantra;
having thus placed the God everywhere, one should place Gāyatrī upon the chest.
Having assigned the eye to the eyes and the weapon to the two hands by means of that very mudrā,
one should then perform the worship of Śiva.
Having purified the place of worship with the Śiva-weapon mantra, once it is fully equipped with offerings, one should thereafter fill the vessel for the arghya water.
Having offered flowers to the Lord of the World in the prescribed order with the Śarva mantra,
one should then remove that floral remains (nirmālya) from his feet using the Astra mantra.
Having thoroughly washed both the liṅga and the pedestal with the auspicious water (śivāmbhas),
and having prepared the arghya as previously described, one should then place the lotus.
One should place Dharma, Jñāna, Vairāgya, and likewise Aiśvarya—
the infinite ones— into the heart in their proper sequence.
The powers (śaktis) should be established in the petals by means of the all-pervading word;
one should establish Manonmanī in the pericarp (karṇikā) in the form of space (vyoma). 19.
Then, having performed the sakalīkaraṇa rite for the omnipresent god Śiva, who is established in the Praṇava,
as before, one should thereafter invoke Śiva.

One should perform the placement with the Sadyojāta mantra established at the feet, and with the Vāmadeva mantra; one should worship for the presence with the Bahurūpa mantra and with the Puruṣa mantra in due order.
Having offered flowers with this instruction, one should place them in the directions;
these are the syllables spoken by Śiva, which indeed exceed those pertaining to Time (Kālātman). 22.
Having established the maṇḍala described by Anantavijaya, which concludes with the Vidyāṅga weapons,
one should worship it according to the rules, both for rites of desire and as a daily obligation.
One should consecrate the scented water for the purpose of bathing with the Sadyojāta mantra;
the garments with the Vāmadeva mantra; and the soft girdle-string with the Aghora mantra.
One should give unguents, necklaces, armlets, and so forth—previously purified with the Astra-mantra and consecrated with the Aghora-mantra. 25.
Honey, clarified butter, curd, milk, incense, food offerings, and lamps—these should be consecrated with the Puruṣa mantra, while the remainder is consecrated with the Īśāna mantra. || 26 ||
For indeed, the [mantras] beginning with Sadyojāta are [worshipped] by their own words;
those of Gāyatrī by the words "hṛdaya" (heart) and so forth; and those of the others by their respective forms. || 27 ||
And worship should be performed by the sovereign with his hearts, separately for each of the eight [deities] beginning with Ananta, in due order, using the eight [mantras]. || 28 ||
Now, the propitiation of the mantras by means of mudrās is described.
One should perform the propitiation of the four limbs of the Vidyā using the Kālakarṇī [mudrā]. || 29 ||
Likewise, the knower of mantras should indeed purify the weapon-mantra of the western quarter with a prostration,
and the remaining Lords of Knowledge (Vidyeśas) with the lotus-mudrā.
When the deity has been thus worshipped, the practitioner should place the mantra to be accomplished—
augmented by the limbs of the Vidyā— within the syllable Om upon the lotus seat.
One should worship the Sādhya mantra to the east of the Aghora weapon, to the west of the Lord (Īśāna),
and to the north of the Pāśupata weapon.
Having always bowed to the Lord of the gods with perfumes, flowers, purifiers, and water-offerings that are pleasing to the mind, one should perform the rite of recitation.
Having performed the recitation as prescribed in the ritual manual, the practitioner, for the sake of accomplishing his goal, should offer it to the deity; others, however, should cease.
The practitioner of mantra should offer the recitation, preceded by the ritual procedure, with scented water using the *sarvamantrādima* mantra, enshrined within the *sampuṭa* enclosure, O Śivā. 35.
You are the protector of the most secret of secrets; accept this recitation performed by us, so that through your grace, may my success be attained according to my desire. 36.
O God, whatever good or evil deed I may ever perform here, O Śaṅkara, destroy that for me as I stand at your auspicious feet. 37.
Śiva is the giver, Śiva is the enjoyer, and Śiva is this entire world;
Śiva performs sacrifice everywhere, and he who is Śiva is indeed myself. 38.
Having thus offered oneself, as well as the recitation and worship with devotion, one should bow the head to the God and dismiss Him, saying, "Forgive me. (39)
Meditating with the *sadyojāta* and other mantras, and with the *virāma-praṇava*,
one should lead the mind to absorption in that [Brahman] by means of the *praṇava* alone.
Thus, with a self-restrained mind, one should worship Lord Śiva even once;
he goes to the supreme abode, which is unattainable by those of undisciplined soul. 41.
Thus ends the eighteenth chapter, on the worship of Śiva, in the Svāyambhuva-sūtra-saṅgraha.
